title: Monogenic Fields of Cryptographic Size
summary: For a monic irreducible $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree $n$ and an integer $c$, we study the palindromic transform $F(x) = x^n f(x + x^{-1} + c)$, which produces a polynomial of degree $2n$. We give a discriminant formula $\operatorname{disc}(F) = f(c+2)f(c-2)\operatorname{disc}(f)^2$, sufficient conditions for the irreducibility of $F$, and a criterion showing that $F$ is monogenic when $f$ is monogenic and $f(c+2)f(c-2)$ is squarefree, together with a matching non-monogenicity criterion. Iterating the transform yields monogenic number fields of degree $2^k n$ from a fixed base polynomial.…
